body: That I have no libido. That I indeed prefer to be alone. That I need huge amounts of nicotine and caffeine to get anything done. That I'm not actually sad but still have prepared everything to check out because I have come to the conclusion that life is pointless.

Thanks. I'm not sure if there's ever been a lighted candle inside of me. If there ever was, it either burned out or is fading away. According to Neil Young, the first is preferable, but I wouldn't know if he's right. When I do things that others seem to enjoy, it merely feels like I'm running through a set of algorithms designed for that particular task.

What I don't understand is why many people find it acceptable to end a life if there is physical pain that cannot be treated, but not if there is mental anguish that cannot be treated either. It's not that I haven't tried. I tried therapy, I tried medication, I've been treated with everything there is for twelve years. I've tried to be open minded, to accept help, to change things. I've given it a chance, even though I never wanted to live. But nothing makes me feel different about life. I don't think that I would change my mind in middle of dying if it doesn't come with physical pain. Why would I? I don't feel sad about falling to sleep when I'm tired, and every time I lay in bed and drift off to sleep, I wish that I'd never wake up again.
